messages:
Alex I.: Quick follow-up from the all-hands infra segment — a few concrete questions so we can share clear next steps. TL;DR: APAC GPU availability, autoscaler behavior during spikes, and customer-facing SLA expectations.

Maria (PM): Thanks Alex — can you list the two highest-priority clarifications we should publish to docs?

Alex I.: 1) Exact GPUs we expect in APAC (region map + rough ETA). 2) Autoscaler fallback rules (when we fall back to smaller model variants vs. throttling vs. bursting to on-demand).

Kyle (Infra Lead): Short answers now: APAC launch will start with V100-equivalent instances in SIN and KIX zones, followed by A10/A30 pools in Q2. ETA: gating on contract + rack delivery, target: "within 8–12 weeks". Not final — ops team to confirm procurement dates.

Devon (SRE): On autoscaler: current policy is tiered — try dedicated capacity pool, then burst to reserved on-demand pool (same perf class), then fall back to a smaller model family if latency SLOs are still at risk. We do *not* throttle by default during a burst — we prefer graceful degradation.

Sara (Capacity): To add: there are two knobs we tune per customer: "burst_to_on_demand: true|false" and "model_fallback_threshold_ms". We should publish recommended defaults for latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive customers.

Jenna (Sales): Important for enterprise customers: when we say "burst to on-demand" does that change billing/metering? Need exact language for contracts.

Kyle (Infra Lead): Yes — bursting to on-demand increments usage at on-demand rates. We'll provide pricing table in the dedicated docs. Action: publish a short matrix showing cost delta for common burst patterns.

Alex I.: Can we get a simple commit: who will own the public doc edits and who will own the internal runbook?

Maria (PM): I'll own public docs copy. Kyle + Sara will own internal runbook and the autoscaler playbook. Devon to vet the runbook for operational run sequences.

Devon (SRE): I'll add an incident playbook section: steps to detect capacity exhaustion, command shortcuts, and the immediate manual mitigations (scale up reserved pools, enable cross-region routing, temp model-level throttles). Snippet we'll include:

```
# quick ops commands (example)
rictl capacity scale --pool=dedicated-sgp --delta=+4
rictl routing set --policy=cross-region-burst --regions=us-west-2
```

Kyle (Infra Lead): One more technical clarification requested during Q: how do we prefer to route customer traffic when APAC is constrained? Answer: prefer same-region routing first, then cross-region to nearest compatible AZ with fallbacks ordered by latency then cost. We will publish the region ordering table.

Sara (Capacity): Note on hardware: the first APAC SKU is Q-manufactured; perf will look like V100->A10 baseline. We recommend customers pin to model versions if they require exact GPU microarchitecture for reproducibility.

Jenna (Sales): Can PMs and sales be looped into the doc preview? We need the customer-facing language tomorrow for a renewal conversation.

Maria (PM): Will do. I'll post the draft in #product-docs and ping sales.

infra-bot: Slides from today's all-hands posted: https://internal.redwood/slides/2026-03-23-infra-capacity.pdf :file_folder:

Alex I.: Thanks all. Action items summary: Maria -> publish public FAQ draft; Kyle & Sara -> internal runbook + pricing delta; Devon -> add ops commands & test playbook; Jenna -> confirm wording for renewals. I'll follow up in 48h with a checklist. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder: create runbook ticket and assign to @Kyle (Infra Lead) and @Sara (Capacity) — ticket #INF-7820 created.

Kyle (Infra Lead): Got it, will accept and start drafting.

Alex I.: Closing thread — please add any missing items. If anyone wants to volunteer to help with testing cross-region failover, ping me.

Maria (PM): volunteering to help test cross-region failover tomorrow morning (09:30 PT).

Devon (SRE): I'll join the test.

Sara (Capacity): I'll coordinate with CloudOps for instance prep.

Jenna (Sales): I'll review the public FAQ after Maria posts.

Alex I.: Awesome — thanks everyone.
